transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Orchid Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Orchid CTO), Aisha Khan (Orchid SRE), Diego Marquez (Orchid Data Eng)

Summary (auto):
- POC scope: shortlist open-source models for a 6-week POC targeting financial analytics NLP tasks (multilingual: EN/ES/HI).
- Success criteria: 95th perc latency < 450ms for <512 tokens, end-to-end F1/accuracy targets per task, hallucination rate below threshold, multilang coverage.
- Benchmarks: run 3-model benchmark (Mistral 7B instruct, Llama-3-13B, Mistral-8x) on 48-hour sample, measure throughput at 50 QPS target and cold/warm cache metrics.
- Next steps: send pricing + security docs, Rafael to build harness, customer to send corpus.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run through objectives and then dive into model selection and benchmarking. Rafael's going to cover the technical harness.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Thanks Maya. Quick context, we process high-volume financial alerts and want to extract entities, sentiment, and a short reasoning summary. We need Spanish and Hindi coverage too, about 20% multi-lang traffic.
[00:34] Tom Reynolds: timeline is tight — stakeholders want an internal demo in 6 weeks and procurement loop of 8 weeks, so POC should show clear signals within three weeks.
[00:50] Rafael Ortiz: got it. Couple clarifying q's, what QPS and avg tokens per request do you expect? Also are you okay with hosted API for phase 1 or do you need private right away?
[01:07] Priya Nair: target steady-state 50 QPS, spikes to 120 QPS. Median request ~120 tokens, 95th around 420 tokens. For phase 1 hosted is fine but we'd like dedicated/reserved if early results meet cost/latency needs.
[01:24] Aisha Khan: network-wise we can do VPC peering but will need an egress window; security team will review SOC2 + KMS support.
[01:38] Maya Chen: that aligns with typical POCs. Success criteria from Redwood side? I'd propose: (1) latency SLO: p95 < 450ms for <=512 tokens on dedicated equivalent; (2) quality: task F1 >= existing baseline (you said current baseline is 0.81 F1?), (3) hallucination less than 2% on golden set, (4) throughput 50 QPS sustained with autoscale. Thoughts?
[02:05] Priya Nair: current F1 is 0.81 yes. Hallucination target 2% is reasonable. Also need to check multilingual parity — Spanish should be within 5 points of English.
[02:20] Diego Marquez: one more: inference cost per 1M tokens is a hard metric for execs. We'll want rough unit economics.
[02:32] Maya Chen: noted. We'll provide cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated vs quantized private.
[02:40] Rafael Ortiz: on models — given budget + multilingual need we typically shortlist open-models that balance throughput and instruction-following: 1) Mistral 7B Instruct (fast, lower cost, strong general performance but potentially lower in-domain nuance), 2) Llama-3-13B (better comprehension, heavier compute), 3) Mistral-8x / Mistral-Instruct-8B variants (midpoint), and optionally 4) Vicuna-like tuned variant or local fine-tune if needed. We also consider quantized 4-bit variants for cost.
[03:15] Priya Nair: curious about hallucination differences across those models, and how they behave on finance text (lots of ticker-like tokens and numeric patterns).
[03:26] Rafael Ortiz: good q. We'll include a hallucination check in the harness: prompt a model with golden facts and adversarial follow-ups, measure contradiction rate. Numeric fidelity usually better in the larger Llama-3 family, but Mistral variants are improving.
[03:45] Tom Reynolds: multilingual — do these models have robust Hindi performance? We need devs to validate that tokenization and subword handling for Devanagari aren't a blocker.
[03:58] Maya Chen: Mistral 7B and Llama-3 both support many languages but quality differs. For Hindi specifically we'll include a separate 200-sample test set. If gaps exist we can suggest small instruction-tuning or retrieval augmentation.
[04:18] Priya Nair: retrieval augmentation is interesting — we have an internal index of facts that could be used to ground responses. How feasible is that in POC?
[04:28] Rafael Ortiz: fully feasible. Redwood supports RAG patterns; for the POC we can run two variants: plain LM and LM+retrieval to quantify hallucination reduction and latency impact. We need your index access or a redacted sample.
[04:44] Aisha Khan: security question — we require KMS integration and audit logs. Do you have SOC2?
[04:52] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood is SOC2 compliant — I'll send the security pack. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and detailed audit logs.
[05:04] Priya Nair: good. Back to benchmarks: what metrics will you measure?
[05:11] Rafael Ortiz: core metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, throughput (QPS), cost per 1M tokens, task-level F1/EM, hallucination rate (contradiction percentage), and multilingual delta (EN vs ES vs HI). We'll run cold-start and warmed KV cache scenarios — note: transcription may say KV cache as KV, sometimes we hear K-V.
[05:34] Tom Reynolds: how long does the benchmark run take?
[05:36] Rafael Ortiz: with your 48-hour sample and 50 QPS target, we can run representative microbenchmarks in 24-48 hours. The full evaluation suite (including human review for hallucination samples) might take 5 business days.
[05:50] Priya Nair: timeline check: if we start next Monday, can you deliver initial benchmark results in two weeks?
[05:57] Rafael Ortiz: yes — build harness this week, run benchmarks week 1, share initial numbers by week 2, then iterate. That fits your three-week demo target for early signals.
[06:10] Diego Marquez: any infra pre-reqs for hosted vs dedicated?
[06:16] Rafael Ortiz: for hosted no infra changes; for dedicated we'll need IP allowlist and capacity planning (GPU instance types) — Rafael: I'll follow up with Aisha on VPC peering windows.
[06:29] Aisha Khan: peering window next Tue-Wed is best. We'll scope network and firewall rules then.
[06:35] Maya Chen: on model selection tradeoffs: Llama-3-13B probably gives best single-model quality but at 2-3x inference cost vs Mistral 7B. If cost is primary we often recommend Mistral 7B with instruction-tuning and RAG. If you need the absolute best reasoning/comprehension, test Llama-3. We can also test a quantized Llama-3 13B 4-bit to see cost/latency lift.
[07:05] Tom Reynolds: any concerns about licensing for open models? We can't ship models with restrictive clauses.
[07:12] Maya Chen: we'll verify license compatibility; most Mistral/Llama inference variants are ok for evaluation but we'll confirm for production usage.
[07:20] Priya Nair: data retention — hosted implies logs retained by vendor; we prefer 30-day retention and option to disable logs.
[07:29] Maya Chen: Redwood hosted can be configured to minimize retention and we have a dedicated offering with guaranteed data isolation. I'll include config options in the security pack.
[07:39] Rafael Ortiz: on evaluation harness specifics — I'll instrument:
- synthetic load generator to simulate 50 QPS + spike patterns,
- per-request token breakdown,
- golden set scoring,
- hallucination adversarial set,
- multilingual buckets, and
- RAG vs baseline runs.
[08:05] Priya Nair: good. Also include cost modeling at the end for 1M tokens and projection for monthly traffic of ~1.2B tokens.
[08:17] Maya Chen: we'll provide unit economics for each model + quantization profile.
[08:22] Diego Marquez: curious about caching — you referenced KV cache earlier; will that change latency numbers a lot?
[08:30] Rafael Ortiz: yes, prefix/KV caching helps for multi-turn sessions and prompt templates. Warm cache numbers can be 30-60% faster depending on sequence reuse. We'll report cold vs warm p95.
[08:44] Tom Reynolds: ok for timelines and owners?
[08:47] Maya Chen: recap of owners: Rafael builds harness and runs benchmark; Priya provides corpus and golden prompts; Aisha coordinates VPC/network; Maya sends docs and pricing. Deliverables: benchmark report, cost sheet, security pack.
[09:02] Priya Nair: sounds good. One more question: if Llama-3 is the winner, what's the typical path to private deployment?
[09:12] Rafael Ortiz: post-POC we typically do a dedicated pilot (reserved pool) and if you need on-prem/private, Redwood Private can be deployed into your VPC with customer KMS and audit logging; that's a 4-8 week project depending on procurement.
[09:28] Tom Reynolds: procurement note — we'll need an estimate of committed vs on-demand costs for dedicated.
[09:33] Maya Chen: will include 3 pricing options in the sheet: hosted pay-as-you-go, dedicated reserved monthly tiers, and private licensing estimate.
[09:42] Aisha Khan: any blockers from our side right now?
[09:44] Priya Nair: we'll pull the sample and define the 50 golden prompts by end of day Friday.
[09:50] Maya Chen: great. Rafael, anything else?
[09:52] Rafael Ortiz: I'll outline benchmark details in a follow-up mail and attach the harness repo link; note that auto-transcription sometimes labels speakers oddly — ignore any "Speaker 2" labels.
[10:04] Maya Chen: thanks all. We'll send the security pack + pricing tomorrow and Rafael will follow up with benchmark plan.
[10:10] Tom Reynolds: thanks, bye.

End of call.
